# JMdict and Ding offline dictionaries

Materia uses JMdict from the Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group (EDRDG), copyright James William Breen and EDRDG. Project and documentation: https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project.html . License: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0, https://www.edrdg.org/edrdg/licence.html . Copies of the full license, project documentation, and original JMdict_e.gz are included here. The JMdict-derived index records remain under CC BY-SA 4.0.

Ding German-English dictionary, copyright 1995–2020 Frank Richter and contributors, hosted at TU Chemnitz: https://www-user.tu-chemnitz.de/~fri/ding/ . Data version 1.9, 2020-12-22. License: GNU GPL version 2 or later. DING-COPYING.txt and DING-README.txt retain the original license and documentation; de-en.txt.gz is the corresponding source of the Ding index records, which remain under GPL-2.0-or-later.

The indexes normalize lookup keys and add reverse English indexes. JMdict headwords/readings, sense restrictions, and English glosses are used; Ding parallel form columns are kept aligned and query keys omit grammatical annotations. Original source archives are provided so that all source data remains available. Counts and source hashes are in manifest.js. Build procedure: scripts/build-language-dictionaries.py. Separate records retain their respective licenses; this directory is a collection of the two datasets.

Supported direct pairs: Japanese ↔ English, German ↔ English. Japanese queries accept kanji and kana. Reverse English lookup matches complete glosses/phrases and may return multiple senses. No direct Japanese–Chinese or German–Chinese dictionary is claimed: Chinese fallback uses exact English gloss matches in ECDICT and is explicitly labeled as an indirect translation, which may omit senses. Long sentences are not machine-translated by these dictionaries.

Updating: download the current JMdict_e.gz from https://www.edrdg.org/pub/Nihongo/JMdict_e.gz and the current de-en.txt.gz from https://ftp.tu-chemnitz.de/pub/Local/urz/ding/de-en/de-en.txt.gz to .local/dictionary-sources, refresh the accompanying upstream documentation/licenses, run scripts/build-language-dictionaries.py and the offline dictionary tests, then rebuild the desktop package. Refresh JMdict at each application release; users can continue using the installed snapshot offline between releases. manifest.js records exact source hashes for reproducibility.
